question: Does the position-target by waiting interaction differ across two frozen visual executors on identical physical prefixes, and is it changed by the first placement control segment?
freeze: Reuse both exact final controller/observer sources from the previous study; no new controller tuning or checkpoint/threshold changes. Development checks the new shared runner, pairing and numerical execution only.
pairing: Every method pair matches initialization, fault and post-hold snapshots exactly. All hold/wait alternatives share the same physical fault prefix. Method orders interleave and rotate.
cost: Every actual RGB acquisition/fit and retry is charged as physical blocking. Reference RGB and renderer warmup are common pre-fault task preparation.
primary: Y500 shared guards at500Hz, unchanged100ms registered-support and10mm penetration thresholds; C and interface remain20Hz. Report originalY20 alongside.

statistics.unit: whole initialization seed retaining sides, both executors and all hold/wait conditions
primary_contrasts: position-by-wait averaged over wrist settings within each executor
executor difference of those position-by-wait effects

conditional_placement.trigger: Original CAD feedback position-by-wait CI lower>0 AND CAD-minus-landmark position-by-wait CI lower>0 AND landmark position-by-wait CI lower<=0. This gates a heterogeneity diagnostic; a CI crossing zero does not establish no effect.
conditional_placement.single_change: In the CAD executor only, replace the two initial visually computed downward targets by two0.09m downward strokes at30steps each, retaining measured-wrist holding, both RGB observations/services,10step loaded holds, and all subsequent release, pickup, recenter and lift logic.
conditional_placement.hypothesis: If the original adaptive placement amplifies sensitivity, replacing only its touchdown target schedule should reduce position-by-wait protection/cost interaction. No formal-test retuning or additional variants.

mechanism: Use only evaluator-side recorded motion/contact and robot/visual ports. Compare registered/measured target offset, hold tracking, wait-end velocity/motion, observed visual-target to handle mismatch, placement, actual first-close geometry, registered grasps and retries. A target/handle mismatch is not a pure object-pose error.
stopping: Complete the960cohort, run only the predeclared240diagnostic if triggered, synchronize paper/reproduction and stop. No new geometries, learned models, gain/contact scans or post-hoc searches for positive results.
